def seed_all(seed:int=42):
    """
    set random seed and cuda related settings for reproducibility
    Args:
        seed: int setting the seed
    Return:
        None
    """
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)
    torch.backends.cudnn.deterministic = True
    torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark = False
#---------------------------------------------
seed_all(settings.RANDOM_SEED)

NOTE on Single Threshold vs Dual Thresholds¶

  • We evaluated all metrics on both real data and generated data
  • To maximize F2-Score, we have thresholds of 0.096 on Real-Data and 0.060 on Generated Data.
  • Rounding this threshold to 1 decimal points we get the same 0.1 threshold, and we may use this as a single threshold

However, in an agentic workflow, we can use 2 thresholds in Triage stage: Our ML classifier-model in anomaly/fraud detection-node calculates initial probability $p(\text{fraud})$ as follow with for exmple 0.15 as low threshold and 0.85 as high threshold like below:

  • $p < 0.15 \rightarrow$ Auto-Approve (Legitimated Transaction)
  • $p > 0.85 \rightarrow$ Auto-Block & Write to LTM as FRAUD_CONFIRMED
  • $0.15 \le p \le 0.85 \rightarrow$ Escalate to LLM Agent

Question: How we can find the optimum values for these 2 thresholds based on our data?¶

  • This will be a 2D optimization problem
  • We need to define some costs and then find low threshold ($\tau\_{low}$) and high threshold ($\tau\_{high}$).
  • Similar to F2-Score on single threshold we consider the cost for False-Negative (FN) twice the cost for False-Positive (FP) due to nature of the consequence for the business as discussed before (in step-1)
  • Also we need to consider a cost for LLM-agent involvement in the process if Fraud detector could not auto-resolve
  • Finally there will be a cost due to accuracy of LLM-agent
  • While selecting these parameter needs many practical considerations in the real production setup, here we simply assume
    1. Cost of FN: 10.0
    2. cost of FP: 5.0
    3. cost of using LLM-Agent: 0.2
    4. LLM-Agent accuracy: 90%
      • Agent Accuracy can also be broken into two to different accuracy recall and precision accuracy
      • For simplicity we assume recall and precision accuracy for LLM-agent are the same
      • We may collect data to find the difference, and re-tune model in future/practical situation
In [23]:
th_log = np.linspace(-5, -0.01, 100)
best_tau_low1, best_tau_high1, result_df, Tau_Low_Log, Tau_High_Log, cost_surface = \

Prepare Data for LTM (vector dB)¶

  • Now we have our optimal dual thresholds
  • Also we have our real-dataset and a sample of generated dataset
  • We will use dual thresholds to label these dataset with
    • TRUE_POSITIVE
    • TRUE_NEGATIVE
    • FALSE_POSITIVE
    • FALSE_NEGATIVE
  • We do not need to add TRUE_NEGATIVE into LTM, but we kept 100 of them as sample in our labeled data

Note:¶

  • Confusion matrix with single thresholds (low and high) and dual thresholds are shown for both real and generated data
  • It is noticeable that in dual thresholds case, the FN and FP are the minimum between single thresholds low and high
  • This means in ideal scenario having two stage refinement (using ML classifier as first stage Detector, then passing uncertain scenario to LLM-Agent) can improve both recall and precision (and better F-Score)

Summary¶

  1. We have our selected ML Binary classifier for Fraud detection
  2. First we find optimal threshold for this classifier on both real dataset and a sample of generated dataset
  3. We explain that in agentic workflow we can use dual thresholds and the ML-classifier as detector can send uncertain cases to LLM-agent
  4. We define some cost values, and find optimal values for dual thresholds
  5. Finally we labeled our datasets to be used in LTM preparation
  6. It is noticeable that using dual threshold and dual stage refinement can improve both recall and precision which will result is better f-score.
